column4: “My taste has gotten heavier” is not a natural English way to express that one’s food preferences have become stronger or richer.

column1: 我的右手是维族的，左手是汉族的。
column2: My right hand is Uighur, and my left is Han.
column4: “My right hand is Uyghur, and my left is Han” is not a natural or coherent Chinese sentence.

column2: My head aches.
column4: 我的头疼 is unnatural here; a native speaker would usually say 我头疼 or 我的头很疼.

column1: 我的家并不是那样的一个大家庭。
column2: My family isn't such a big family.
column4: “我的家”通常指房子或住所；这里要表达 family，宜说“我的家庭”或“我家”。

column2: My family is very proud of me.
column4: “为我很骄傲” is unidiomatic; say “为我感到骄傲” or “以我为傲”.

column2: My brother is a teacher.
column4: 弟弟 specifically means younger brother; the English does not specify his age relative to the speaker.

column2: My room is just above.
column4: “My room is just above” sounds incomplete here; “My room is just upstairs” is natural.

column1: 我的房间很舒适,即使它小了一点。
column2: My room is comfortable, if it is a little small.
column4: “Comfortable, if it is a little small” is awkward and unclear; “even though it is a little small” matches the Chinese.

column1: 我的手提包，一只是大的，另一只是中号的。
column2: One of my suitcases is large, and the other one is medium.
column4: 手提包 means handbag, not suitcase.

column2: my cell phone
column4: This is a noun phrase, not a sentence.

column2: My phone is out of battery.
column4: “Out of battery” is not idiomatic; say “out of charge” or “the battery is dead.”

column1: 我的手表每天都会多快一分钟。
column2: My watch gains one minute a day.
column4: “多快一分钟”不自然；应说“我的手表每天会快一分钟”。

column2: Where are my watches?
column4: 手表 is singular here; the English asks where multiple watches went.

column1: 我的文件在那个箱子里。
column2: My papers were in that box.
column4: The Chinese says the papers are in the box, not that they were there.

column2: My friends don't play tennis.
column4: 我的朋友 is singular or unspecified in number, while “my friends” is plural.

column2: My lover is great at cooking.
column4: 爱人通常指配偶或伴侣；“my lover”通常带有情人或婚外恋的含义。

column1: 我的父母准备买一个新的光盘。
column2: My parents are going to buy a new CD.
column4: “一个光盘” is not the natural measure phrase; use “一张光盘” or “一片光盘”.

column2: My life was worthless.
column4: “没有意义” means “has no meaning” in the present, not “was worthless.”

column2: My eyes hurt a little.
column4: “我的眼”不自然地指“my eyes”; say “我的眼睛有点儿疼。”

column1: 我的眼睛和头都哭疼了。
column2: My eyes and head hurt from crying.
column4: “哭疼了” is unnatural here; say “哭得眼睛和头都疼了”.

column1: 我的祖母做了一套新衣服给我。
column2: My grandmother made me a new dress.
column4: 一套新衣服 means a new outfit or set of clothes, not specifically a dress.

column2: my teacher
column4: This is a noun phrase, not a sentence.

column2: I was always good at English.
column4: “一直都不错” means the speaker’s English has been good all along, typically up to now; “I was always good at English” can imply that is no longer true.

column2: What are my responsibilities?
column4: The Chinese asks about one responsibility, while the English asks about multiple responsibilities.

column2: My height surpasses yours.
column4: “我的身高比你高” is an unnatural comparison; say “我比你高” or “我的身高比你的高.”

column2: My car's in the shop.
column4: “在店里修理中” is awkward; a more natural phrasing is “正在店里修理” or “送去修了”。

column2: I believe what he said is fact.
column4: “What he said is fact” is ungrammatical; it should be “what he said is a fact.”

column1: 我相信他采取的行动是对的。
column2: I believe that his action was in the right.
column4: “His action was in the right” is unnatural English; say “his action was right” or “he was right to take that action.”

column1: 我相信你会做的很棒的。
column2: I'm sure you'll do great.
column4: “做的很棒” should be “做得很棒.”

column1: 我相当有自信我能做到这一点。
column2: I'm fairly confident I can do that.
column4: 相当有自信我能做到这一点 is awkward; a natural phrasing is 我相当有信心能做到这一点.

column1: 我看电视度过了星期六的下午。
column2: I spent Saturday afternoon watching entirely too much TV.
column4: The English adds “entirely too much,” which is not expressed in the Chinese.

column2: Let's see if I can tomorrow.
column4: “能不能” has no stated action, so the sentence needs context to be translated.

column2: I couldn't sleep.
column4: “我睡不著”表示现在睡不着；“I couldn't sleep”表示过去没能睡着。

column2: I am going to sleep.
column4: 我睡觉了 indicates that the speaker went to bed or is now sleeping, not that they are going to sleep.

column1: 我知道你的感情受伤了。
column2: I know your feelings are hurt.
column4: “你的感情受伤了” is unnatural; say “你的感情受到了伤害” or “你受伤了”.

column1: 我知道我知道它，但我想不起来了。
column2: I know that I know it, but I can't remember it.
column4: “我知道我知道它” is awkward and unnatural; the repeated “知道” does not work naturally with “它” here.

column2: I knew this was wrong.
column4: 我知道 means “I know,” not “I knew.”

column1: 我知道这里会发生什么。
column2: I know what can happen here.
column4: 这里会发生什么 means what will happen here, not what can happen here.

column2: I know, your busy too.
column4: “your” should be “you're.”

column2: I'm sure that was her.
column4: The English specifies a past identification (“that was her”), which the Chinese does not.

column2: I felt an impulse to cry out loud.
column4: The Chinese says the speaker suddenly really wants to shout, while the English puts that feeling in the past.

column2: I did it for the first time.
column4: 我第一次做到 is awkward as a standalone sentence; a more natural phrasing is 这是我第一次做到。

column2: I can't play tennis very well.
column4: “打的” should be “打得” in this sentence.

column2: My stomach hurts—maybe bad food.
column4: “Maybe bad food” is a fragment; a natural translation is “Maybe I ate something bad.”

column2: I could answer all the questions.
column4: 能 expresses ability in the present here; “could” suggests past ability.

column1: 我能在哪里乘上机场巴士？
column2: Where do I get an airport bus?
column4: “乘上机场巴士” is unnatural here; say “坐机场巴士” or “乘机场巴士”.

column2: Can I help you at all?
column4: “什么么” is an incorrect repetition; say “我能帮你们什么吗？”.

column2: I was able to help her.
column4: “我能帮助她” expresses ability in the present or generally, not that you were able to help her in the past.

column1: 我能用英文表达我的意思。
column2: I could make myself understood in English.
column4: “我能” means “I can,” while “I could” usually refers to past ability or a hypothetical situation.

column2: I paid five dollars for the book.
column4: 五元 means five yuan, not five dollars.

column2: I was very impressed by his story.
column4: “被他的故事感染了”是受到故事感染或触动，不等于“被故事深深打动/留下深刻印象”。

column2: I'm getting online harassment.
column4: “I'm getting online harassment” is unnatural; say “I'm being harassed online.”

column2: I want a little bottle of water.
column4: “一瓶小水” is unnatural; say “一小瓶水” for “a small bottle of water.”

column2: I want to buy.
column4: “我要买了” means “I’m going to buy it now” or “I’m about to buy it,” not simply “I want to buy.”

column1: 我要告诉你的只能你我知道。
column2: What I'm about to say is strictly between you and me.
column4: The wording is awkward; a natural version would be 我要告诉你的事只能你我知道。

column2: I must say good-bye to you.
column4: 我要 expresses intention or a future action here, not the obligation implied by “must.”

column2: I'm going to miss that.
column4: “我要失去它了” means “I’m going to lose it,” not “I’m going to miss that.”

column2: It'll take a long time.
column4: 我要花很长时间 means “I’ll spend a long time,” with 我 as the subject; the English says that it will take a long time.

column2: I see you found your bag.
column4: “我见你找到了你的包” is unnatural in Mandarin; “我看见你找到你的包了” is natural.

column2: I felt bad.
column4: “我觉得不好了” is not a natural way to say “I felt bad.”

column1: 我觉得什么都不说是最好的。
column2: I found it best to say nothing about the matter.
column4: “我觉得” means “I think,” not “I found”; the English also adds “about the matter.”

column2: I thought you said something.
column4: 中文是“我觉得你说了什么”，而英文是“我以为你说了什么”。

column1: 我觉得很难用一天就做完这么多的工作。
column2: I don't think it's possible to finish that amount of work in one day.
column4: 中文说觉得很难完成，英文说认为不可能完成，语气更绝对。

column2: I don't think this is correct.
column4: “这不是真的” means “this isn't true,” not specifically “this isn't correct.”

column2: I don't have a good feeling about this.
column4: “我觉得这没什么好” is incomplete or unnatural as a standalone sentence; “我觉得这没什么好的” would be natural.

column1: 我觉得这部电影值得一看再看。
column2: I think it is worthwhile to see this film twice.
column4: “一看再看” means watching again and again, not specifically twice.

column1: 我认为我知道那意味着什么。
column2: I think that I know what this means.
column4: 那 means “that,” but the English says “this.”

column1: 我认为这些问题很容易。
column2: I thought the questions were easy.
column4: 我认为 means “I think,” while “I thought” puts it in the past.

column2: I think I'll stay.
column4: “我认” is incorrect here; it should be “我认为” or “我想”。

column1: 我认识胡安，我们是同事。
column2: I know John – we're colleagues.
column4: “胡安” is Juan, not John.

column2: I remember seeing you last year.
column4: “看过你” is unnatural here; “见过你” is the usual expression for having met or seen someone.

column2: I think I've told you.
column4: “我记得” means “I remember,” while “I think” expresses uncertainty.

column1: 我记得在哪儿听到过那首音乐。
column2: I remember hearing that music somewhere.
column4: “首”通常量词用于歌曲或曲子，不用于“音乐”；“那段音乐”更自然。

column2: I treat you to a cup of coffee.
column4: 我请你喝杯咖啡 is an offer or promise to treat someone to coffee, not the habitual-sounding “I treat you.”

column1: 我读过许多现代作家的作品。
column2: I have read many modern authors.
column4: The Chinese says the speaker has read works by many modern authors; the English says they have read the authors themselves.

column2: I don't recognize anyone.
column4: 我谁也不认识 means “I don’t know anyone,” not “I don’t recognize anyone.”

column2: I succeeded in getting what I wanted.
column4: “赢得了我想要的”不自然地表达“got what I wanted”；通常说“得到了我想要的”。

column2: I walked to school.
column4: 我走路到学校 describes walking to school, not specifically in the past; the English says “I walked.”

column2: I am talking to you about history.
column4: The Chinese says you’ll tell someone a bit of history; the English says you are talking to them about history.

column2: I talked to her.
column4: “我跟她谈了话” is unnatural phrasing; “我跟她谈过话” or “我跟她谈了谈” is more natural.

column2: I am nearly as tall as she.
column4: 我跟她近一样高 is unnatural; say 我跟她差不多一样高.

column1: 我过会儿再跟你们一起。
column2: I'll join you all later.
column4: 我过会儿再跟你们一起 is incomplete; it needs an action, such as 一起去 or 一起玩.

column2: I am not good at sports.
column4: “我运动不好”不自然；表达不擅长体育运动通常说“我不擅长运动”。

column1: 我还是一个小男孩的时候就住在这里。
column2: I've lived here since I was a boy.
column4: 中文只说小时候住在这里，没有说一直住到现在；英文表达了从小时候持续至今。

column2: I still have to sleep for a while.
column4: 我还要再睡一会儿 means “I’m going to sleep a little longer,” not that I have to.

column2: I made a desk of wood.
column4: “造一张木桌子”搭配不自然；通常说“做一张木桌子”。

column2: I invited her to dinner.
column4: “邀了她一起晚餐” is not natural; say “邀请她一起吃晚饭” or “邀她共进晚餐.”

column1: 我邻居今天吵架了，一直吵到警察过来。
column2: My neighbors had a fight today, which lasted until the police came.
column4: The Chinese says “my neighbor” (singular), but the English says “my neighbors” (plural).

column2: I missed that bus.
column4: 车 does not specify a bus; the English adds that detail.

column2: I must go out.
column4: “我需要” means “I need to,” not necessarily “I must.”

column2: I was very, very lucky.
column4: The Chinese says “I am very lucky,” while the English says “I was very lucky.”

column2: Sooner or later, he will know.
column4: “或早或晚”不自然；通常说“迟早”或“早晚”。

column1: 房子前头是花园，后头是树林。
column2: Garden in front, woods behind.
column4: The English is a fragment, not a complete sentence.

column2: placeholder-p3
column4: “placeholder-p3” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: Everybody is alive.
column4: “所有人都是活着的” is unnatural; say “所有人都活着.”

column1: 所有人都有享有国籍的权利。
column2: Everyone has the right to a nationality.
column4: “都有享有” is an unnatural, ill-formed combination here.

column1: 所有小孩都听老师的话。
column2: All of the children are listening to the teacher's words.
column4: 听老师的话 usually means obey or do as the teacher says, not simply listen to the teacher's words.

column2: All the teachers were in the pub.
column4: 在酒吧 describes where the teachers are, not where they were.

column2: Open your book to page nine.
column4: “打开你的书到第九页” is unnatural. A native speaker would say “把书翻到第九页.”

column2: Open your heart.
column4: “打开你的心胸” is unnatural; “敞开心扉” is the idiomatic expression.

column2: I'm disturbing you.
column4: 打扰了 is an apology or polite way to get someone’s attention, not a statement that you are disturbing them.

column2: Hand in a bibliography of your sources.
column4: “书目提要” refers to an annotated or descriptive bibliography, not simply a bibliography of sources.

column2: Tie the rope firmly.
column4: “口袋” means “pocket,” not “rope.”

column1: 护士给病人打针、发药物。
column2: Nurses give shots and medicine.
column4: “发药物” is an unnatural collocation here; say “给病人发药” or “给病人发药品”.

column2: It's no use worrying about it.
column4: “担心它是没有用的” is unnatural; say “担心它也没用” or “担心是没有用的。”

column1: 拍完那部电影，他一下子就出名了。
column2: He became very famous soon after that movie came out.
column4: 拍完那部电影 means after he finished filming that movie, not after the movie came out.

column1: 控制一个班级需要你做老师的所有技能。
column2: To control a class calls for all your skills as a teacher.
column4: “需要你做老师的所有技能” is unnatural; it should say that managing a class requires all of a teacher’s skills.

column1: 控制自己会说的语言可不简单呀！
column2: It's not easy to control the languages that you can speak!
column4: 控制自己会说的语言 is an unnatural way to express controlling which languages you speak.

column1: 推迟的每一分钟都是有生命代价的。
column2: Every minute of delay costs lives.
column4: “推迟的每一分钟都是有生命代价的” is unnatural phrasing. A natural version is “每延迟一分钟都要付出生命代价。”

column2: Hold your horses, young man.
column4: “握住你的马” is a literal translation of the English idiom, not a natural Chinese expression.

column2: Search; find; discover!
column4: This is a list of words or commands, not a sentence.

column2: Catch a signal.
column4: The Chinese is a context-dependent fragment, while the English is phrased as an imperative.

column2: placeholder-p2
column4: “placeholder-p2” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder”不是这句话的英文翻译。

column2: The government strongly backs eco-protection.
column4: “Eco-protection” is not a natural English expression here; “environmental protection” is more idiomatic.

column2: The regime is stable and society harmonious.
column4: “society harmonious” is ungrammatical; it needs a verb, such as “society is harmonious.”

column1: 政治家从来不告诉我们他们的别有用心。
column2: Politicians never tell us their inner thoughts.
column4: “别有用心”指怀有不可告人的动机，不是“inner thoughts”。

column2: The witch hunt has begun.
column4: “政治迫害” means political persecution, not a witch hunt.

column1: 教法语的是怀特老师，不是格林老师。
column2: French is taught by Mr White, not by Miss Green.
column4: The Chinese says “Teacher White” and “Teacher Green” without specifying gender, but the English adds Mr. and Miss.

column1: 数学和英语是我最喜欢的两门学科。
column2: Math and English were my favorite subjects.
column4: The Chinese describes the subjects as favorites now, while “were” puts that in the past.

column2: Maths is taught on Tuesdays.
column4: “安排在星期二” says the class is scheduled for Tuesday, while “is taught on Tuesdays” suggests a recurring schedule.

column1: 整晚一会下雨，一会停雨。
column2: It was raining on and off all night long.
column4: “停雨” is awkward here; a natural phrasing is “一会儿下雨，一会儿停.”

column2: Mind your language.
column4: “文明用语” is a slogan-like phrase rather than a complete sentence.

column2: New people, new laws.
column4: “新人新法律” is not a natural Chinese expression in this context.

column2: placeholder
column4: “新想法不断生成” is unnatural; “新想法不断产生” or “涌现” is more idiomatic.

column1: 新来的秘书一分钟可以打七十几个字。
column2: The new secretary types about 70 words per minute.
column4: “七十几个字”指七十多个字（汉字），不是每分钟约七十个英语单词。

column1: 旁边一排衣服跟这里的衣服没什么不一样。
column2: There is no difference between this row of clothes and the one next to it.
column4: The Chinese compares the row beside it with the clothes here; the English compares this row with the one next to it.

column2: Countless stars twinkle in the sky.
column4: “星星在天空闪” is not natural here; say “星星在天空闪烁”.

column1: 无论多难，都要坚持到底。
column2: No matter how hard, persist to the end.
column4: “No matter how hard” is incomplete here; the English needs to specify what is hard.

column1: 无论结果会是怎样，我也不会改变我的计划。
column2: Whatever results may follow, I will carry out my plan.
column4: 中文说无论结果如何都不会改变计划；英文说会继续执行计划，含义不完全相同。

column2: The Japanese are an industrious people.
column4: 日本人是勤奋的国民 sounds unnatural; a more natural phrasing is 日本人很勤奋.

column1: 早知如此，就不应该借钱给他。
column2: You should have known better than to lend him money.
column4: The Chinese means “Had I known this, I shouldn’t have lent him money,” not “You should have known better.”

column2: Extended by an hour.
column4: The English is a fragment; it needs a subject, such as “It was extended by an hour.”

column2: When will tomorrow arrive?
column4: 中文通常是在问某人明天几点到；英文则是在问“明天”什么时候到。

column1: 明天去野餐，我们要不要买一些水果、零食什么的？
column2: We are going on picnic tomorrow. Shall we buy some fruits, snacks, and so on?
column4: “Going on picnic” is ungrammatical; say “going on a picnic.”

column2: Tomorrow we all can go.
column4: “Tomorrow we all can go” is awkward English; “We can all go tomorrow” is natural.

column2: 7 o'clock p.m. tomorrow evening
column4: This is a time fragment, not a sentence.

column2: I need to have a meeting tomorrow.
column4: The Chinese says there is a meeting tomorrow; it does not say that the speaker needs to have one.

column1: 明天，一定要给我打电话。
column2: Mind you call me up tomorrow.
column4: “Mind you call me up tomorrow” is not a natural way to say this; “Be sure to call me tomorrow” would be natural.

column2: How old will you be next year?
column4: “你会是几岁” is unnatural; a natural phrasing is “你明年多大？”

column2: Wednesday at 9 o'clock a.m.
column4: This is a time phrase, not a sentence.

column2: On Saturday you do physical education.
column4: “Do physical education” is unnatural here; say “have PE” or “take physical education.”

column2: Sunday at 10:30 a.m.
column4: This is a time phrase, not a sentence.

column2: Flowers in spring, fruit in autumn.
column4: The English is a pair of fragments; it should say something like “Flowers bloom in spring, and fruit ripens in autumn.”

column1: 春节是一年里最大的节。
column2: Spring Festival is the biggest festival of the year.
column4: “最大的节” is not a natural way to say “the biggest festival”; use “最大的节日.”

column2: Were you at home yesterday?
column4: 不在家吗 asks “Weren’t you at home?”; the English omits the negative.

column1: 昨天太冷了，我只好待在家里。
column2: It was so cold yesterday I stayed home.
column4: “只好” means the speaker had no choice but to stay home; the English only says they stayed home.

column2: Yesterday was cloudy.
column4: “昨天是多云” is unnatural; say “昨天多云.”

column2: 7:30 yesterday evening
column4: This is a time fragment, not a sentence.

column2: Yesterday it was a little too hot.
column4: 有一点热 means “a little hot,” not “a little too hot.”

column1: 昨天的台风把树刮倒了。
column2: The tree had been blown down by the typhoon of the day before.
column4: “Had been blown down” places the event before another past event, which the Chinese does not indicate.

column1: 昨天要视天气好的话，我们就会去动物园了。
column2: If the weather had been nice yesterday, we would have gone to the zoo.
column4: “要视” is not grammatical here; it should be “要是”.‌

column1: 昨晚你把她送回家了吗？
column2: Did you drive her home last night?
column4: “送回家” means took or saw her home, but does not specify driving.

column1: 昨晚睡觉之前家里进了小偷。
column2: Last night my house was robbed while I was still awake.
column4: The Chinese says a thief entered the house before bedtime; the English says the house was robbed while the speaker was still awake.

column1: 是你准备好茶的时候了。
column2: It's about time you got the tea ready.
column4: This phrasing is unnatural; a native speaker would more likely say 你该准备茶了.

column2: Yes, I am Xiaoyu. Who are you?
column4: 你呢？ means “And you?” or “What about you?”, not specifically “Who are you?”

column2: It's easy to distinguish good from evil.
column4: “是非对错” means right and wrong, not good and evil.

column2: Obviously, he was wrong.
column4: 显然，他错了 means “Obviously, he is wrong” or “Obviously, he was mistaken”; the English implies a past error.

column1: 晚上六点到上午八点在家。
column2: I'm at home from six o'clock in the evening to eight o'clock in the morning.
column4: The Chinese gives no subject, while the English specifies “I.”

column1: 晚餐之后你才可以看电视。
column2: You can watch TV after supper.
column4: 才 means you can watch TV only after supper; the English omits that restriction.

column2: She studied Japanese after dinner.
column4: The Chinese describes a habitual or present action, while the English says she studied in the past.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not an English translation.

column1: 更多投资在教育的钱将会刺激经济成长。
column2: More money for education will spur economic growth.
column4: “更多投资在教育的钱” is awkward and ungrammatical; say “更多投在教育上的钱.”

column2: There's been an accident.
column4: “曾经有一个意外”表示曾经发生过一次意外，不等同于“There's been an accident.”

column2: Shame on you guys.
column4: 中文是替对方感到羞愧，英文“Shame on you guys”是在斥责对方。

column1: 最大可能假想事故什么时候会发生？
column2: When will the most probable hypothetical accident occur?
column4: “最大可能假想事故” is an unnatural, unclear phrase in Chinese.

column1: 最好的理发师是同性恋。
column2: The best hairdressers are gay.
column4: The Chinese refers to the best hairdresser (singular), while the English makes a general claim about hairdressers (plural).

column2: No one has seen him recently.
column4: The Chinese leaves the subject implicit; it does not say that no one has seen him.

column1: 月亮已从地平线升起了。
column2: The moon was above the horizon.
column4: The Chinese says the moon has risen above the horizon; the English describes only its position.

column1: 有一个穿过树林的小路。
column2: There is a path through the wood.
column4: “一个小路” uses the wrong measure word; say “一条小路.”

column1: 有一些漂亮的花在花瓶。
column2: There are some beautiful roses in the vase.
column4: “在花瓶” is missing a location word such as “里”; the Chinese is ungrammatical. Also, “花” means flowers, not specifically roses.

column2: I want to go to America someday.
column4: “我要去” says that the speaker will go, not that they want to go.

column1: 有个男人开门走了出来。
column2: The door opened and a man came out.
column4: The Chinese says the man opened the door; the English only says the door opened.

column1: 有个问题想请教您，可以吗？
column2: I have a question I want you to answer. Can you?
column4: “Can you?” is incomplete and unnatural here; the Chinese asks whether it is okay to ask the person a question.

column1: 有了我，我们已经多一个人了。
column2: And with me, we are yet one more.
column4: “And with me, we are yet one more” is unidiomatic English.

column1: 有些情况之下，这条规则不能成立。
column2: There are some cases where the rule does not hold good.
column4: “Does not hold good” is an unnatural phrasing here; say “does not hold” or “does not apply.”

column1: 有什么事是我该做的吗？
column2: Is there anything I must do?
column4: “该做”表示应该做，英文的“must do”语气更强，表示必须做。

column2: Did you do something fun?
column4: The Chinese asks whether there is anything happy or good happening; the English asks whether you did something fun.

column1: 有什么是你不能证明确相信的呢？
column2: What do you believe is true even though you cannot prove it?
column4: “证明确相信” is not grammatical or natural Chinese.

column2: The department made the document public.
column4: “有关部门”指相关部门（通常为复数或泛指），不是特指的单个部门。

column2: How many arithmetic books are left?
column4: “算数书”用词不当，通常说“算术书”；整句可说“还剩多少本算术书？”

column2: I don't know if there's time.
column4: “有时候不知道的” means something like “sometimes [I] don’t know,” not “I don’t know if there’s time.”

column2: Sometimes I can't help myself.
column4: 办不了 means unable to manage or do something, not unable to help oneself.

column1: 有时候盟军无法避免战争。
column2: Sometimes the Allies could not avoid battle.
column4: The Chinese says the Allies cannot avoid war, while the English puts this in the past (“could not”) and says “battle.”

column1: 有时我们必须回望过去，才能看清前程。
column2: Sometimes we need to look back to know where we are going to.
column4: “Where we are going to” is incomplete here; it should be “where we are going” or “where we are headed.”

column2: The weather promises to clear up.
column4: “有望会变晴” is awkward; “有望转晴” or “有望变晴” is more natural.

column1: 有没有人要养可爱的小猫？
column2: Is there anyone who wants to keep the cute kitten?
column4: “可爱的小猫” is generic, while “the cute kitten” refers to a specific kitten.

column2: There were risks.
column4: “有风险” means there are risks; it does not specify that the risks were in the past.

column2: You're the boss.
column4: “服了你了” means something like “I give up” or “You amaze me,” not “You’re the boss.”

column2: Bin lived in Singapore.
column4: 本 is pronounced Běn, not Bin.

column2: The temperature has stayed hot this week.
column4: 气温通常说“很高”，而不是“很热”；可以说“天气很热”。

column1: 村子里的每个人都认识他。
column2: Everybody in the village knew him.
column4: The Chinese says everyone knows him, while the English says everyone knew him.

column2: Let's take advantage of the long weekend.
column4: “大周末” is not a natural expression here; “长周末” is commonly used for “long weekend.”

column2: A love letter from Gray?
column4: 这是一个缺少完整句子结构的片段。

column2: The pistol misfired.
column4: 枪走火了 means the gun went off accidentally, not that it misfired.

column2: There's a branch on the tree.
column4: “一根枝” is unnatural here; say “一根树枝” or “一根枝条”.

column2: placeholder-p1
column4: “placeholder-p1” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: Judge by the evidence.
column4: “根据依据” is redundant and unnatural; say “根据证据来判断” or “依据证据来判断”.

column2: Whose dictionary is it on the table?
column4: The English is awkward and ungrammatical; it should be “Whose dictionary is on the table?”

column1: 桌子下面和底下都很干净。
column2: Under the table it is clean.
column4: “下面”和“底下” mean nearly the same thing, so using both this way is unnatural.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” does not translate the Chinese sentence.

column1: 此制图员出名于其制图的精准性。
column2: This cartographer is famous for the precision in his maps.
column4: “出名于其制图的精准性”不自然；可说“因制图精准而出名”。

column1: 此前我父亲从没出过国。
column2: My father has never been outside the country until now.
column4: 此前我父亲从没出过国 says he had never been abroad before then; it does not imply he has gone abroad now.

column1: 此地为两军再次交战之地。
column2: That was where the two armies would fight again.
column4: 此地 means “this place,” but the English says “that was.”

column1: 死一个人是悲剧；死上万人是数据。
column2: A single death is a tragedy, a million deaths is a statistic.
column4: “万人” means ten thousand people, not a million.

column2: What was the time of death?
column4: This is an incomplete question fragment.

column2: Mother has gone shopping.
column4: “去了逛街” is not natural Mandarin; say “去逛街了”.

column1: 母亲常说时间就是金钱。
column2: My mother often said that time is money.
column4: 常说 means “often says,” but the English says “often said.”

column1: 每个国家都有它们自己的文化与习俗。
column2: Every country has its own culture and customs.
column4: 每个国家与它们搭配不自然；通常说“每个国家都有自己的文化与习俗”。

column2: Every child likes an apple.
column4: “苹果” refers to apples in general, not “an apple.”

column2: All cops are bastards.
column4: The sentence contains an offensive insult.

column1: 每吃一个苹果就跳一下。
column2: Jump once for each apple you ate.
column4: The Chinese describes jumping each time an apple is eaten; the English refers specifically to apples already eaten.

column1: 每天早上我养成看电视英语课程的习惯。
column2: Every morning I make it a rule to watch the English course on TV.
column4: “看电视英语课程” is awkward; say “看电视上的英语课程”.

column2: The match paused five minutes.
column4: “The match paused five minutes” is ungrammatical here; say “The match paused for five minutes.”

column2: Graduating is like losing your job.
column4: “等同于失业”是等同于没有工作，不是“失去工作”。

column1: 民众比较支持新的就业政策。
column2: The public rather supports the new employment policy.
column4: “Rather supports” is an unnatural way to express support in this sentence.

column2: Water drips down.
column4: “水一滴一滴地落” is unnatural; say “水一滴一滴地滴下来。”

column2: The reservoir stores much water.
column4: “水库存了很多水” is not a natural way to say this; use “水库里存了很多水” or “水库蓄了很多水.”

column2: Water has three forms.
column4: “形” is not natural here; say “形态” for water’s three forms.

column2: The flood harmed many people.
column4: “水灾害了不少人” is not a natural way to say the flood harmed many people.

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” does not translate the Chinese sentence.

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column1: 水道如树枝般越过了平原。
column2: The waterways branch out across the plain.
column4: “越过了平原” means crossed the plain, not branched out across it.

column1: 汤米不会回答最后一个问题。
column2: Tommy couldn't answer the last question.
column4: “不会” expresses inability in the present or future, but “couldn't” places it in the past.

column1: 没有一个人能做到这一点。
column2: No one man could do it.
column4: 没有一个人 means “no one”; “no one man” suggests that no single man could do it.

column1: 没有了我的眼镜我几乎看不到。
column2: I can hardly see without my glasses.
column4: “没有了我的眼镜” is unnatural in this sentence; say “没有我的眼镜，我几乎看不到.”

column2: No one will know.
column4: “能知道” means “can know,” not “will know.”

column2: There's no more salt.
column4: 没有再多的盐了 is unnatural; say 没有更多的盐了 or 没有盐了。

column2: There were no more free seats.
column4: 没有更多免费座位了 describes the current situation, not a past one.

column2: That won't work!
column4: “没用的” means “useless” or “of no use,” not “That won’t work.”

column1: 没钱，没工作，没朋友，他真是无所适从。
column2: No money, no job, no friends. He was truly at loose ends.
column4: “无所适从”是指不知该怎么办，不是“at loose ends”。

column2: Coastal areas are developed.
column4: The Chinese says the coastal areas have developed economies; the English only says the areas are developed.

column2: The court reviewed the lawsuit.
column4: “审查这个官司” is unnatural; a court would usually “审理这个案子”.

column2: The mud is soft.
column4: “泥土” means soil or earth, not mud.

column2: I have almost finished my work.
column4: The Chinese says the work is almost finished, while the English specifically says that I have almost finished it.

column2: I got a low score on the test.
column4: “测试我考了低分”语序不自然；可以说“我测试考了低分”或“我在测试中考了低分”。

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not an English translation.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not an English translation.

column2: Ships anchor in the bay.
column4: The Chinese describes ships currently anchored in the bay; the English describes ships anchoring there as a general or repeated action.

column2: The seaside is damp with good air.
column4: “Good air” is unnatural here; “fresh air” would be more idiomatic.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not an English translation.

column2: The lake was frozen.
column4: “湖冻冰了”不自然；通常说“湖结冰了”。

column2: The lake is very deep.
column4: “湖水的深度很大” is unnatural; a native speaker would more naturally say “湖水很深”.

column2: beautiful clothes
column4: This is a noun phrase, not a sentence.

column2: Volcanic ash disrupted air travel.
column4: “航运” refers to shipping or navigation, not air travel.

column2: The rocket entered orbit.
column4: “火箭发射进入了轨道” is not a natural way to say the rocket entered orbit.

column2: The train has sleepers.
column4: “Sleepers” usually means people who sleep; “sleeping berths” is the natural translation here.

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” does not translate the Chinese sentence.

column2: a boisterous bar
column4: This is a noun phrase, not a sentence.

column2: placeholder-p6
column4: “placeholder-p6” is not a valid English translation.

column2: Love is only an invention.
column4: “爱不过是发明”表达不自然；通常会说“爱情不过是一种发明”。

column1: 爱和被爱是世上最幸运的事。
column2: Loving and being loved are the most joyful things in the world.
column4: “最幸运” means “the luckiest,” not “the most joyful.”

column2: Love loves love.
column4: “爱爱爱” is a fragment rather than a complete, natural sentence.

column2: The father is good.
column4: “父亲是好的” is unnatural as a standalone sentence; “父亲很好” or “父亲是个好人” would be natural.

column2: Dad has never smoked cigarettes.
column4: “一直都不抽烟” means Dad does not smoke or has consistently not smoked; “has never smoked” specifically claims he has never smoked at any point.

column1: 爸爸去北京出差已经两天了。
column2: It has already been two days since dad went to Beijing on business trip.
column4: “On business trip” is missing an article; say “on a business trip.”

column1: 爸爸建议今天下午去看电影。
column2: Father suggested to go to the movies this afternoon.
column4: “Suggested to go” is ungrammatical here; say “suggested going” or “suggested that we go.”

column2: dad's car
column4: This is a noun phrase, not a sentence.

column2: I've brushed my teeth (already).
column4: 牙刷过了 does not naturally mean “I've brushed my teeth”; say 我刷过牙了.

column2: Cows provide us with good milk.
column4: “好奶” is not a natural way to say “good milk”; use “好牛奶” or “优质牛奶.”

column2: play very happily
column4: Both sides are verb phrases, not complete sentences.

column1: 现代年轻人戴风帽是装一种派头。
column2: Currently, having a hood is part of young people's fashion.
column4: “戴风帽是装一种派头” is not natural Mandarin phrasing.

column1: 现在只看他们会不会帮忙了。
column2: It all depends on whether they will support us.
column4: “帮忙” means help; the English adds “support us,” which is more specific.

column1: 现在很难静下心来好好看一本书。
column2: It is presently very difficult to calm down and treat oneself with a book.
column4: “Treat oneself with a book” is not a natural English expression for reading a book.

column2: It is exactly three o'clock now.
column4: “三时正” is unnatural in ordinary Mandarin; “三点整” is the usual phrasing.

column1: 现在是我一直往最坏的方面想。
column2: I'm jumping to the worst-case scenario.
column4: “现在是我一直……” is an unnatural sentence structure here.

column2: It's time to wait now.
column4: “现在是时候等着了”不自然；可以说“现在该等着了”或“现在是等待的时候了”。

column2: It's now windy.
column4: “It's now windy” is awkward English; “It's windy now” is natural.

column2: Now, let’s go back to where we were.
column4: “话再说回来” is not a natural expression here; “话说回来” would be natural.

column2: Jane filled out an application.
column4: “一张申请书” is an unnatural measure-word choice; “一份申请书” would be natural.

column1: 珍略过了她无法回答的问题。
column2: Jane skipped the questions she couldn't answer.
column4: “珍略过了” is not a natural or correct way to say “Jane skipped”; the name or wording appears to be wrong.

column2: Ideals are the driving force forward.
column4: “The driving force forward” is unnatural English; say “the driving force behind progress.”

column2: Life is indeed a good thing.
column4: “生命确实是好的东西” is awkward; a native speaker would more naturally say “生命确实是好东西”.

column1: 生日的时候，我们会吃蛋糕，还要送礼物。
column2: During a birthday, we eat cake and also give presents.
column4: “During a birthday” is unnatural here; say “On birthdays” or “For birthdays.”

column2: angrily say
column4: Both sides are verb phrases, not complete sentences.

column1: 生活很艰苦，但他很坚强。
column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: Life is hard.
column4: 生活是难的 is unnatural here; a native speaker would usually say 生活很难.

column2: Do you need to wash fresh vegetables?
column4: 生菜 means “lettuce,” not fresh vegetables in general.

column2: Brew tea with boiling water—fragrant leaves.
column4: “用开水做茶” is not a natural way to say “brew tea”; say “用开水泡茶”.

column1: 电影制作是一个令人兴奋的工作。
column2: Movie making is an exciting job.
column4: “一个……的工作” uses an unnatural measure word here; say “一份令人兴奋的工作.”

column2: The movie is almost about to start.
column4: “Almost about to start” is awkwardly redundant; say “The movie is about to start” or “The movie will start soon.”

column2: How many people were in the cinema?
column4: The Chinese asks how many people are in the cinema, while the English asks how many people were there.

column2: Broken computers need repair.
column4: “修复电脑” is unnatural for repairing a broken computer; “修理电脑” is more idiomatic.

column1: 电话公司上个月切了我的线。
column2: The phone company cut me off last month.
column4: “切了我的线” is not a natural way to say the phone company cut off service.

column1: 电话响起时，他跑去接起。
column2: When the phone rang, he ran to answer it.
column4: “接起” needs an object here. “他跑去接电话” is natural.

column2: Nice guys finish last.
column4: The Chinese says women love bad men; “Nice guys finish last” has a different meaning.

column2: The boy drinks milk.
column4: 在喝 means he is drinking now, not that he habitually drinks milk.

column1: 男孩登上了梯子，向上爬了起来。
column2: The boy seized the ladder, and began to climb.
column4: “登上了梯子” means climbed onto the ladder, not seized it.

column2: The boy observed the birds all day.
column4: “观察了一整天鸟”不自然；可以说“观察鸟观察了一整天”。

column2: Artists illustrate.
column4: 画家画画 means “Painters paint”; “illustrate” is more specific.

column2: Stay there.
column4: “这里” means “here,” but the English says “there.”

column2: The climb reached the peak.
column4: “登山到了高峰” is not a natural way to say the climb reached the peak.

column2: A picture is worth a thousand words.
column4: 百闻不如一见 means seeing something once is better than hearing about it many times, not that a picture is worth a thousand words.

column2: Compared with last year, great progress.
column4: “Compared with last year, great progress” is a sentence fragment.

column1: 看到这些作业，我毫无压力。
column2: Seeing those tasks, I did not feel the burden.
column4: The Chinese says the speaker feels no pressure, while the English says they did not feel burdened.

column2: I want to sleep.
column4: 睡过去通常 means to pass out or fall asleep, which is stronger than simply wanting to sleep.

column2: The truth will clear soon.
column4: “The truth will clear soon” is not natural English; say “The truth will soon become clear.”

column2: Tears flowed down.
column4: “Tears flowed down” is unnatural English; tears usually “rolled” or “streamed down.”

column2: After sleep the mind is clear.
column4: “After sleep the mind is clear” is awkward English; “After waking up, the mind is clear” is more natural.

column2: Those who count their blessings experience more joy.
column4: “知足者常乐”是知足的人常常快乐，不是数算自己的福气。

column2: Hard to finish in the short term.
column4: “Hard to finish in the short term” is a sentence fragment.

column1: 石头被美丽得放置在日式庭园里。
column2: Rocks are beautifully arranged in the Japanese-style garden.
column4: “美丽得放置” is ungrammatical here; use “美丽地放置” or “被美丽地摆放”.“

column2: The auditorium is full.
column4: The Chinese says there are many people in the auditorium; it does not say the auditorium is full.

column1: 神话和传说应该一代一代的传承下去。
column2: Myths and legends should be handed down from generation to generation.
column4: 这里应写“地”： “一代一代地传承下去”。

column1: 神话让我们能透悉古文明。
column2: The myth offers insights into the ancient civilization.
column4: “透悉” is an incorrect word here; “深入了解” or “洞悉” would be natural.

column1: 离我远点儿！我现在烦得很！
column2: Stay away from me! I'm very stressed right now!
column4: 烦得很 means very annoyed or irritated here, not very stressed.

column2: Leaves fall in the autumn.
column4: “秋天秋叶落” is awkward and repetitive; a natural phrasing would be “秋天树叶落” or “秋叶在秋天落下.”

column1: 科学发明并不总是使世界变得更美好。
column2: Scientific discoveries don't always make the world a better place.
column4: “科学发明”是 scientific inventions，不是 scientific discoveries。

column1: 科学家处理大多数物理的事物。
column2: Scientists deal mainly with physical matters.
column4: “大多数物理的事物” is unnatural phrasing in Chinese.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” does not translate the Chinese sentence.

column1: 科技那么发达，什么都是有可能的。
column2: Science and technology is so developed. Anything is possible.
column4: “Science and technology” takes “are,” not “is.”

column2: Renting needs a deposit.
column4: “Renting needs a deposit” is unnatural; say “You need to pay a deposit when renting.”

column2: The air conditioner has got out of order.
column4: “Has got out of order” is unnatural here; say “has broken down” or “is out of order.”

column2: Dress up.
column4: 穿上衣服 means “put on your clothes” or “get dressed”; “dress up” suggests dressing formally or for a special occasion.

column2: Is laughter a quality of man only?
column4: “Is laughter a quality of man only?” is awkward and unnatural English; “Is laughter unique to humans?” would be more natural.

column2: Wait for me until I write you.
column4: 中文是“我一到就给你写信”，英文却说“等我写信给你再……”。

column2: Simply unbelievable!
column4: 简直不敢相信 means “I simply can’t believe it,” not “simply unbelievable.”

column1: 米以公斤为单位来出售。
column2: Rice is sold by the kilogram.
column4: “米以公斤为单位来出售” is unnatural; a native speaker would say “米按公斤出售” or “米是按公斤卖的”.

column1: 精神的健康和身体的健康一样重要。
column2: Mental health is as important as physical health.
column4: “精神的健康”不自然；通常说“心理健康”或“精神健康”。

column2: A red light is the stop sign.
column4: “Stop sign” usually means a physical road sign, not the signal conveyed by a red light.

column1: 经济危机使很多公司倒闭了，也使很多人失去了工作。
column2: The financial crisis caused lot of companies to go out of business and also caused many people to lose their jobs.
column4: “Caused lot of companies” is ungrammatical; it should be “caused a lot of companies.”

column1: 经理打算改良公司的结构。
column2: The manager wants to improve the company's structuring.
column4: “The company's structuring” is awkward; “the company’s structure” is natural.

column1: 结婚以后，你想跟父母一起住吗？
column2: Do you want live together with your parents after you get married?
column4: The English is missing “to”: “Do you want to live together with your parents…?”

column2: When the light is green, cars turning must yield to pedestrians.
column4: “拐弯车” is unnatural here; “转弯车辆” is more idiomatic.

column2: Internet is very slow.
column4: “Internet is very slow” needs an article; say “The internet is very slow.”

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” does not translate the Chinese sentence.

column1: 翻译这本书要花一些时间。
column2: It would take some time for me to translate this book.
column4: The Chinese does not say that it would take time for the speaker to translate the book; it states generally that translating it will take some time.

column1: 老人去世了，大家都很难过。
column2: The old man passed away and everyone grieved.
column4: “老人” does not specify that the person is male, but “old man” does.

column2: The old man looked wise.
column4: “明智” usually describes a decision or action, not a person; “老人看起来很有智慧” would sound more natural.

column1: 老师检验了我们的作业。
column2: The teacher checked our homework.
column4: “检验作业” is not a natural way to say the teacher checked homework; “检查” or “批改” is appropriate.

column1: 老师生病了，但是她还是来上课了。
column2: The teacher is sick, but she still come to class.
column4: “She still come” should be “she still comes” or “she still came.”

column2: teacher's friend
column4: This is a noun phrase, not a sentence.

column2: The teacher lectures vividly.
column4: “Lectures vividly” is an unnatural phrasing; say “gives lively lectures.”

column2: The teacher awarded him a prize.
column4: “赏给他一个奖” is an unnatural way to say that he was awarded a prize.

column1: 老板不同意，我没办法帮你。
column2: The boss didn't agree, so I have no way to help you.
column4: 不同意 means “doesn’t agree” here, not “didn’t agree.”

column1: 老板现在很生气，什么人也不见。
column2: The boss is very angry. He's doesn't want to see anybody.
column4: “He's doesn't” is ungrammatical; use “He doesn't.”

column2: the friends that the boss invites / invited
column4: This is a noun phrase, not a complete sentence.

column1: 老板通常比较关注结果，不是过程。
column2: The boss usually pays more attention to results and not process.
column4: The natural phrasing is “pays more attention to the results, not the process.”

column1: 考试接近了，要认真准备。
column2: The exam is近; prepare well.
column4: “The exam is近” contains the Chinese word “近” and is not grammatical English.

column2: Meat or fish?
column4: This is a context-dependent choice fragment, not a complete sentence.

column2: Shareholders hold much stock.
column4: “Hold much stock” is unnatural here; “hold a lot of stock” or “hold many shares” would be more natural.

column2: The stock account is at the bank.
column4: “股票的账户” is an unnatural phrasing; a native speaker would say “股票账户”.

column2: Ken has never visited Kyoto.
column4: “参观京都” is unnatural for visiting a city; use “去过京都” or “游览京都.”

column2: Ken wasn't running.
column4: 肯没跑步 is not a natural way to write “Ken wasn’t running”; the name is rendered awkwardly.

column2: I felt her gaze from behind.
column4: This is a fragment with no stated or recoverable subject for “felt.”

column2: Juan is 35 years old today.
column4: 今年 means “this year,” not “today.”

column2: Can you tell us a bit more about that?
column4: The Chinese asks to tell “me” more, but the English asks to tell “us.”

column2: I'm glad I could help.
column4: The Chinese says it is great to be able to help; the English adds that the speaker is glad they helped in the past.

column2: Understand yourself.
column4: This is a fragment meaning “can understand yourself,” not a complete sentence or natural standalone command.

column1: 能说给我听你的地址吗？
column2: Can you tell me your address?
column4: “说给我听你的地址”不自然；应说“能告诉我你的地址吗？”

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column1: 脾气不好的人总是最晚获知任何讯息。
column2: Irritable men are always the last to know about things.
column4: “人” is gender-neutral, but “men” specifically refers to males.

column2: Self-help is the best help.
column4: “自助是最好的帮助” sounds like a direct translation and is not a natural Chinese expression.

column1: 自此之后，他过着艰难的生活。
column2: Since then, he lives a tough life.
column4: “Since then” calls for a perfect tense here, such as “has lived” or “has been living.”

column1: 至于应该做什么，我和他的见解不同。
column2: My view was different from his as to what should be done.
column4: The Chinese says their views differ, while the English says his view was different in the past.

column2: As for the result, unknown yet.
column4: “As for the result, unknown yet” is a sentence fragment.

column2: Good medicine is bitter to the mouth.
column4: “Bitter to the mouth” is unnatural English; the idiom is “Good medicine tastes bitter.”

column1: 艺术有很多种类，绘画、舞蹈、电影以及文学等都是艺术。
column4: The English translation is missing.

column2: Fireworks on the festival.
column4: “Fireworks on the festival” is a fragment; say “Fireworks are set off during the festival.”

column2: It took me a while to get up.
column4: The word order is unnatural; say 我花了一段时间才起床.

column2: Pinyin uses letters.
column4: The Chinese says English has 26 letters; the English says Pinyin uses letters.

column1: 英语不是他的母语，他说得倒挺地道的。
column2: English is not his mother language, but he speaks quite native-like.
column4: “Mother language” and “speaks quite native-like” are unnatural; say “native language” and “speaks quite naturally/like a native speaker.”

column2: Apples have sold-out!
column4: “Apples have sold-out” is ungrammatical; “sold out” is not hyphenated here, and the phrasing is unnatural.

column2: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
column4: “获人赠马” is not a natural way to say “receive a horse as a gift”; use “受人赠马” or “送的马.”

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column1: 虽然这次他很努力，但最后还是失败了。
column2: After all his efforts, he also failed this time.
column4: The Chinese says that although he worked hard this time, he still failed; the English changes that contrast to “after all his efforts” and “also.”

column1: 衣服和服装店都在二层。
column2: Clothes and clothing stores are on the second floor.
column4: 衣服和服装店都在二层不自然；衣服不能像店铺一样说“在二层”，除非指具体的衣服。

column1: 表面上他很静，内心很紧张。
column2: Calm on the surface, nervous inside.
column4: The English is a fragment rather than a complete sentence.

column1: 西面大楼的扩建在研究中。
column2: The expansion of the building's west end is being studied.
column4: 西面大楼通常 means the building to the west, not the west end of a building.

column1: 要做蛋糕，你要用到鸡蛋，黄油和糖。
column2: To make a cake, you need egg, butter and sugar.
column4: “You need egg” is unnatural in this list of ingredients; “eggs” would be natural.

column1: 要关心孩子的心理健康。
column2: Mind children's mental health.
column4: “Mind children's mental health” is unnatural here; “Care about children's mental health” is more natural.

column1: 要想身体健康，就应该多锻练身体。
column2: If you want to keep healthy, you should do more exercises.
column4: 锻练 is an incorrect character choice; the standard spelling is 锻炼.

column1: 要是他知道会发生什么，他就会改变计划。
column2: Had he known what was about to happen, he would have changed his plan.
column4: “会发生什么” means what would happen; it does not say it was about to happen.

column1: 要是你能在那里就好了。
column2: I wish you could have been there.
column4: The Chinese expresses a wish that you could be there, while the English refers to having been there in the past.

column1: 要是当时有好好读说明书就好了。
column2: If only I read the user manual properly.
column4: For the past counterfactual, say “If only I had read the user manual properly.”

column1: 要是我能去音乐会就好了。
column2: If only I can go to the concert!
column4: “要是我能去……就好了” expresses a wish, so the English should say “If only I could go,” not “If only I can go.”

column1: 要看东京的景物只花几天时间是很难的。
column2: It is hard to see the sights of Tokyo in a few days.
column4: The sentence is awkwardly phrased; a more natural version is “只花几天时间很难看完东京的景点。”

column2: Keep exercising long-term.
column4: “Keep exercising long-term” is awkward; say “Keep exercising over the long term.”

column1: 解决问题最简便的方法往往是最好的办法。
column2: The simplest solutions are always the best.
column4: The Chinese says the simplest method is often the best; the English says the simplest solutions are always the best.

column2: placeholder
column4: “捕住了强盗” is an unnatural collocation; “抓住了强盗” or “逮捕了强盗” is more natural.

column1: 警察给小偷看了监控，小偷只好承认了。
column2: The police showed the surveillance to the thief, so he had to admit it.
column4: “Showed the surveillance” is unclear; the English should refer to surveillance footage.

column2: Police keep community safety.
column4: “Keep community safety” is not natural English; say “maintain safety in the community” or “keep the community safe.”

column2: The police investigated responsibility.
column4: “追究了责任” means held someone accountable or pursued responsibility, not simply investigated responsibility.

column2: carefully listen
column4: Both sides are verb phrases, not complete sentences.

column2: Let's be friends with birds.
column4: “做鸟类的朋友” sounds unnatural in Chinese; a native speaker would more naturally say “和鸟类做朋友”.

column2: Let us back in.
column4: “让我们回去” means “Let’s go back,” not “Let us back in.”

column2: It disappointed me.
column4: The Chinese omits the subject, so who or what disappointed the speaker is unclear without context.

column2: Keep this lesson in mind.
column4: “记好了这教训” is unnatural; a natural phrasing is “记住这个教训.”

column2: Remember to admire her new dress.
column4: 称赞 means to praise or compliment her dress, not simply admire it.

column1: 记忆是我们大脑的一种主要功能。
column2: Memory is an essential function of our brain.
column4: “主要功能” means a main function, not necessarily an essential one.

column1: 许多战士会战中挂彩了。
column2: Many soldiers were wounded in the battle.
column4: The Chinese sentence is ungrammatical; “会战中” does not work here.

column2: The exam questions are not difficult.
column4: “试题” and “题目” overlap in meaning here, making the sentence awkwardly redundant.

column1: 该有人告诉她真实情况。
column2: She deserves to know the truth.
column4: The Chinese says someone should tell her the truth; it does not say that she deserves to know it.

column2: Said and done.
column4: “Said and done” is not a natural or accurate English translation of 说到做到.

column2: Let's tell the truth.
column4: 说实话 is an instruction to tell the truth, not “Let's tell the truth.”

column2: Talk is cheap.
column4: “说得简单” means “say it simply” or “put it simply,” not “talk is cheap.”

column2: Tell me about it.
column4: 说来听听 means “Tell me” or “Let me hear it,” not the idiomatic “Tell me about it.”

column2: Making eye contact when speaking is polite.
column4: 说话看人礼貌 is unnatural Chinese for saying that making eye contact while speaking is polite.

column1: 说都说了，就别说这是什么秘密了。
column2: Say what you want to say, just don't spill secrets.
column4: “说都说了” means it has already been said, not “say what you want to say.”

column2: Keep us updated.
column4: “给我们更新” is an unnatural way to say “keep us updated”; “向我们更新情况” is more natural.

column2: Please introduce yourselves.
column4: “自己” is singular here, but “yourselves” is plural.

column2: Can you show me the way please?
column4: “给我指点一下” means give me some guidance, not show me the way.

column2: Please submit the homework.
column4: “补交作业” means to submit overdue or make-up homework, not simply to submit homework.

column2: Will you let me have a go?
column4: “让我一下” usually means “make way for me” or “give me a moment,” not “let me have a go.”

column2: Please keep your opinion.
column4: “请保留你的意见” sounds unnatural as a standalone request; “保留意见” usually means to reserve judgment.

column1: 请取好你的东西再下车。
column2: Please take your belongings before getting off.
column4: “取好你的东西” is not a natural way to say “take your belongings”; “拿好” or “带好” would be more idiomatic.

column1: 请告诉我下一步该做什么。
column2: Please show me what to do next.
column4: 告诉 means “tell,” not “show.”

column2: Turn back, please.
column4: “请回来” means “Please come back,” not “Turn back, please.”

column2: Please come again in three days' time.
column4: “三天内回来” means “come back within three days,” not specifically “in three days’ time.”

column1: 请我可以今晚开一开你的汽车吗？
column2: May I borrow your car tonight?
column4: “请我可以” is ungrammatical here. A natural version is “我今晚可以借一下你的车吗？”

column2: Please tell the truth.
column4: “事实” means “the facts,” not “the truth.”

column1: 请把他确实的地址告诉我。
column2: Tell me exactly where he lives.
column4: “确实的地址” is unnatural here; “确切的地址” would be more idiomatic.

column2: Write the address in detail.
column4: “把地址写详细” is unnatural; say “把地址写详细点.”

column2: Please turn down the radio.
column4: “关小声点” is not a natural way to say “turn down”; say “把收音机的声音调小点” or “把收音机开小声点.”

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” does not translate the Chinese sentence.

column2: Measure the weight and amount.
column4: “重量和量”搭配不自然；通常说“重量和数量”。

column2: Please speak slower.
column4: “满点” is incorrect here; it should be “慢点” (speak more slowly).

column2: Please sit.
column4: “请用座”用错了字；应为“请坐”。

column2: Leave your address for contact.
column4: “For contact” is unnatural English; say “so we can contact you.”

column2: Please wait a little while longer.
column4: 稍等一会儿 means “wait a little while”; “longer” adds the idea that the person has already been waiting.

column2: Please go on the left, not the right.
column4: “Go on the left” is unnatural here; “Please go to the left, not the right” would be more natural.

column2: Where is the stage door?
column4: “剧场后门” means the theater’s back door, not specifically the stage door.

column1: 请问最后一次开信箱在什么时间？
column2: Excuse me, when was the mailbox last opened?
column4: “最后一次开信箱在什么时间” is awkwardly phrased; “最后一次是什么时候打开信箱的？” is more natural.

column1: 请问河南中路五十二弄在什么地方？
column2: Excuse me, where is 52 south river street?
column4: 河南中路 means Henan Middle Road, not South River Street.

column2: Excuse me, what time is it?
column4: “现在什么时候” is not a natural way to ask the time; say “现在几点？”

column2: Readers increased.
column4: “Readers increased” is unnatural; say “The number of readers increased.”

column2: The number of readers is increasing.
column4: “数目在增” sounds incomplete here; “读者的数目在增加” is more natural.

column1: 读这样的书会对今后的生活会有用。
column2: Read such books as will be useful in later life.
column4: The sentence repeats “会”; remove one instance.

column2: No one was there.
column4: The Chinese says no one is there, while the English says no one was there.

column2: No one can deny the fact.
column4: “否定其事实”搭配不自然；通常说“否认这个事实”或“否定这个事实”。

column2: Nobody watches her.
column4: 没在看她 means nobody is watching her now; “Nobody watches her” suggests a general or habitual situation.

column2: Who and who are classmates?
column4: “Who and who are classmates?” is not natural English; say “Who are classmates?” or “Which two people are classmates?”

column2: Who helps her?
column4: 谁帮帮她？ asks who can help her, while “Who helps her?” asks who helps her generally.

column2: Who wants a piece of cake?
column4: “想要来一块蛋糕” is unnatural in this context; say “想来一块蛋糕”.

column1: 谁来为风险投资提供资金？
column2: Who will provide capital for the venture?
column4: 风险投资 means “venture capital,” while “the venture” refers to a business undertaking.

column2: Who was here?
column4: “谁来了这里？” asks who came here, not who was here.

column2: Who organized that meeting?
column4: 这次 means “this meeting,” not “that meeting.”

column2: Who's your favorite teacher?
column4: “诗” is a wrong character here; it should be “是”.

column2: Whoever said so, it is false.
column4: “谁这么说说得不对” is not grammatical or natural Chinese.

column2: It is you that are to blame for it.
column4: 责任应该由你来负 means the responsibility should be yours; it does not necessarily say you are to blame.

column2: Fees cover room and board.
column4: “住和吃” is not a natural way to say room and board; “食宿” or “住宿和餐饮” would be more idiomatic.

column2: Let's go out now. It isn't raining any more.
column4: “没在下雨了” is not a natural way to say that it has stopped raining. Say “不下雨了” or “雨停了”.

column2: Get on the bus quickly!
column4: 上车 means get into/on a vehicle; it does not specify a bus.

column2: Just do it!
column4: 赶紧 conveys urgency: “Hurry up and do it!” The English omits that urgency.

column1: 距离村内的邮政局不到一公里。
column2: It was less than one kilometer to the village post office.
column4: The Chinese is a context-dependent fragment with no stated subject or point of reference.

column2: There are no cars on the street.
column4: 没什么车 means there are few cars or little traffic, not that there are no cars.

column2: We met heavy rain on the way.
column4: “Met heavy rain” is not a natural English expression; say “encountered heavy rain” or “got caught in heavy rain.”

column1: 踢球是我的最喜欢的运动。
column2: Football is my favorite game.
column4: “踢球是我的最喜欢的运动” is unnatural; say “踢球是我最喜欢的运动”.

column2: She wanted to help them.
column4: “过去” says this was in the past, but the English does not include that information.

column2: The games closed.
column4: “The games closed” is not a natural way to say that a sports meet has ended.

column2: Sweating from exercise is good.
column4: The Chinese says sweating from exercise is good for your health; the English omits the health benefit.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: The weather is nice recently.
column4: “The weather is nice recently” is unnatural; say “The weather has been nice lately.”

column2: Can you still do it?
column4: 还可能吗 means “Is it still possible?” The Chinese doesn’t say “you” or “do it.”

column2: Thanks anyway.
column4: 中文表示“还是应该说谢谢”，而英文是直接表达“不过还是谢谢你”。

column2: There are still two stops left.
column4: 还有两站下去 is not a natural way to say there are two stops left.

column1: 这一带的方言使用者数量居多。
column2: Speakers of the dialect are in the majority in this region.
column4: “使用者数量居多”搭配不自然；可说“方言使用者占多数”。

column1: 这一年他在学习上有很大的进步。
column2: This year, he improved greatly on the education front.
column4: “On the education front” is an awkward, unnatural way to express progress in his studies.

column2: I don't agree with you on this point.
column4: “这一点我不赞成你”搭配不自然；可以说“这一点我不同意你的看法”。

column2: placeholder-p14
column4: “placeholder-p14” is not an English translation.

column1: 这世上还有很多东西是吉理不明白的。
column2: Ziri still has much to learn in this world we live in.
column4: The Chinese says there are many things Ziri does not understand, not that Ziri has much to learn.

column2: I haven't been busy for the past few days.
column4: 这两天 means “these two days” or “these days,” not specifically “the past few days.”

column2: How many US dollars is this?
column4: “How many US dollars is this?” is unnatural; ask “How much is this in US dollars?”

column2: This thing is special.
column4: “特” cannot be used this way; say “特别”.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column1: 这个价格把运费包括在内。
column2: The fee includes tax.
column4: The Chinese says the price includes shipping, not that the fee includes tax.

column1: 这个周末你可以抽点时间教我法文吗？
column2: Will you have a little time this weekend to help me with my French?
column4: 教我法文 means “teach me French,” not merely “help me with my French.”

column1: 这个国家被长期的战争毁坏了。
column2: The country had been devastated by long war.
column4: “By long war” is ungrammatical; say “by a long war” or “by prolonged war.”

column1: 这个家庭有个五岁的女孩。
column2: This family has a five year old child.
column4: 中文明确说是女孩，英文只说是孩子。

column2: This project is at its mid-stage.
column4: “工程在中期”不自然；可说“工程处于中期阶段”。

column2: Here is a pan without handles.
column4: The Chinese says this pan has no handle; the English adds “Here is” and refers to multiple handles.

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese.

column2: This craft is exquisite.
column4: “手工艺品很精” is not a natural way to say the craft is exquisite; “很精美” would be natural.

column1: 这个新的市场可能改良全部的工业。
column2: This new market may improve the entire industry.
column4: “改良全部的工业”搭配不自然；通常会说“改善整个行业”。

column2: What happened that night?
column4: “这个晚上” means “this evening,” not “that night.”

column1: 这个月我只打算在明天一天做那件事。
column2: Tomorrow is the only day this month I plan to do that.
column4: “在明天一天” is unnatural; say “明天这一天” or simply “明天”.

column2: This style looks nice.
column4: “这个样” is not natural here; say “这个样子” or “这种样式”.

column2: This song is nice.
column4: 歌曲通常量词用“首”；应说“这首歌很好听”。

column2: The party was, on the whole, successful.
column4: 真成功 means “really successful”; “on the whole” adds a qualification not present in the Chinese.

column1: 这个玩具是用木头做的。
column2: That toy is made of wood.
column4: “这” means “this,” while the English says “that.”

column1: 这个班的每个学生都很聪明。
column2: Each of the students in this class are very smart.
column4: “Each” takes a singular verb: “Each of the students in this class is very smart.”

column1: 这个男孩实际上是要去做。
column2: The boy actually was going to do it.
column4: “做”后缺少宾语，句子听起来不完整；这里应说“做这件事”或“去做它”。

column1: 这个男孩有一张红润的脸。
column2: The boy had a red face.
column4: The Chinese says the boy has a rosy face; the English says he had a red face.

column2: This necklace has pearls.
column4: The Chinese says the gift has pearls; the English says it is a necklace.

column1: 这个箱子太大了，我的包装不下。
column2: This box is too big to fit in my bag.
column4: “包装”是包装材料或包装过程，不是“bag”；这里应说“我的包装不下”以外的表达，如“我的包放不下”。

column2: What do you call this flower?
column4: “花” takes the classifier “朵” here: “这朵花叫什么名字？”

column2: This dish is a little too spicy.
column4: 有点辣 means “a little spicy”; it does not say the dish is too spicy.

column2: This clock is mine.
column4: “表” usually means a watch here, not specifically a clock.

column1: 这个议案合符我们的政策内容。
column2: This measure is in accord with our policy.
column4: “合符” is not a natural way to say “in accord with”; use “符合” or “合乎”.

column1: 这个词分裂成了两部分。
column2: This word split into two parts.
column4: “分裂” is unnatural for a word splitting into parts; “分成了两部分” is more natural.

column2: placeholder-p5
column4: “placeholder-p5” is not an English translation.

column1: 这个课文太难了，我不想学。另外，我也没准备。
column2: This lesson is too difficult and I don't want to read it. Besides, I didn't prepare for it.
column4: “不想学” means “don't want to study,” not specifically “don't want to read it.”

column1: 这个购物中心在前面一英里远的地方。
column2: This shopping mall is one mile ahead.
column4: “在前面一英里远的地方” is awkward; a natural phrasing is “在前面一英里处”.

column2: placeholder
column4: “这个问题很广泛” is unnatural; say “这个问题涉及面很广.”

column1: 这个问题是隐私的，最好不要问。
column2: This question is private. You'd better not ask.
column4: “这个问题是隐私的” is unnatural; say “这是个私人问题” or “这个问题涉及隐私。”

column1: 这个问题有多方面的原因。
column2: This has many-sided causes.
column4: “Many-sided causes” is not natural English; say “There are many reasons for this.”

column1: 这个问题的根本原因广为人知。
column2: The underlying causes of the problem are widely known.
column4: The Chinese refers to one fundamental cause, while the English refers to multiple underlying causes.

column2: This item is his responsibility.
column4: “项目” means a project, not an item.

column1: 这个饮料的味道很明显是茶的味道。
column2: This drink's flavor is obviously that of tea.
column4: The wording is awkwardly repetitive; a more natural phrasing would be “这个饮料喝起来明显是茶味。”

column2: How disgusting!
column4: “这么恶心的！”不自然；可以说“这么恶心！”或“太恶心了！”

column1: 这么晚了，总不会出了什么事吧？
column2: It's getting late. Do you think something bad might have happened?
column4: “总不会……吧” expresses an expectation that nothing happened, but the English asks whether something bad might have happened.

column2: These books are his treasures.
column4: “这些书是他的宝” is unnatural; “这些书是他的宝贝” is more idiomatic.

column1: 这些书里没有一本是有用的。
column2: None of those books are useful.
column4: The Chinese says “these books,” while the English says “those books.”

column1: 这些人共同的目标是把这个项目做成功。
column2: Their common aim was to make the project successful.
column4: The Chinese states their aim in the present; the English says it was their aim.

column2: How can these people so loud?
column4: “How can these people so loud?” is ungrammatical; it needs a verb, such as “How can these people be so loud?”

column2: Are these your daughters?
column4: 这些人 means “these people,” not “these daughters.”

column2: These goods are Chinese and foreign.
column4: “这些商品有中外的” is awkward and incomplete-sounding; a native speaker would more naturally say “这些商品有国内的，也有国外的。”

column1: 这些汽车在日本制作了。
column2: These cars are made in Japan.
column4: “这些汽车在日本制作了” is ungrammatical; say “这些汽车是在日本制造的。”

column2: Those photos are hers.
column4: “这些” means “these,” not “those.”

column1: 这些还不足以说明问题。
column2: This isn't enough to explain it.
column4: “这些” means “these,” but the English says “this.”

column1: 这件上衣是有名的牌子。
column2: This top is a famous brand.
column4: 这件上衣是有名的牌子 is unnatural; say 这件上衣是有名牌子的 or 这是一个有名的牌子。

column2: This was unexpected.
column4: “在计划之外” means “outside the plan,” not necessarily “unexpected.”

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: It's hard to believe.
column4: “很难以相信的” is not a natural construction; say “很难相信” or “难以置信.”

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: This clothing is totally hideous!
column4: “This clothing” is unnatural here; say “This piece of clothing” or “This outfit.”

column1: 这件衣服只要七八十块钱。
column2: This clothing only costs seventy to eighty kuai.
column4: “This clothing” is unnatural here; say “This item of clothing” or “This garment.”

column2: How much is this clothing?
column4: “This clothing” is unnatural for a single item; say “How much is this piece of clothing?”

column1: 这件衣服虽然是名牌，但是质量却不怎么样。
column2: Although this clothing is brand-name, the quality is not so good.
column4: “This clothing is brand-name” is unnatural English; “This is a designer/brand-name item” would be more natural.

column1: 这件衣服，我喜欢得不得了。
column2: I absolutely love these clothes.
column4: The Chinese refers to one garment; “these clothes” is plural.

column2: How much is this T-shirt?
column4: 衬衫 means “shirt,” not specifically “T-shirt.”

column2: I can't sell at this price.
column4: “我不卖” means “I won’t sell,” not “I can’t sell.”

column1: 这份工作没什么挑战性。
column2: I don't get enough challenge in this job.
column4: “I don't get enough challenge” is unnatural English; say “I don't get enough of a challenge in this job.”

column1: 这位建筑师显然是一位无微不至的建筑师。
column2: You can see that the architect paid scrupulous attention to detail.
column4: Calling the architect “a meticulous architect” with 无微不至的建筑师 is unnatural Chinese.

column1: 这位模范工人得了称号。
column2: This model worker earned a title.
column4: “模范工人得了称号” is unnatural: 模范工人 is already a title or designation, so saying the person got a title is unclear.

column1: 这位母亲偶尔会重温她的儿子的信件。
column2: The mother occasionally reread her son's letter.
column4: The English describes a past rereading of one letter, while the Chinese describes an occasional habit and refers to letters.

column2: That's not entirely wrong.
column4: 这倒也没错 means “That’s not wrong either” or “That’s actually not wrong”; “not entirely wrong” suggests it is partly wrong.

column2: There used to be a shop here.
column4: “有所商店” is ungrammatical; say “有家商店” or “有个商店”.

column1: 这公司主要做进口货物的生意。
column2: That company deals mainly in imported goods.
column4: 这公司 means “this company,” not “that company.”

column2: This pair of shoes doesn't fit me.
column4: “不合我的脚” is unnatural here; a native speaker would typically say “这双鞋不合脚.”

column1: 这只不过全是个大误会而已。
column2: It's all just a big misunderstanding.
column4: “只不过全是个……而已” is an awkward construction; a natural version is “这只不过是个大误会而已。”

column2: This is just chance.
column4: “This is just chance” is unnatural English; “This is just a coincidence” is more natural.

column2: That's just my imagination.
column4: “幻想” means a fantasy or illusion; “my imagination” adds a possessive and does not match the Chinese closely.

column2: That dog is big.
column4: 这只狗 means “this dog,” not “that dog.”

column2: that cat
column4: 这只猫 means “this cat,” not “that cat.”

column1: 这台机器的性能很稳定。
column2: This machine performs stably.
column4: “Performs stably” is unnatural; say “operates stably” or “is reliable.”

column1: 这台电脑你用多少钱买的？
column2: How much was your new computer?
column4: The Chinese asks how much this computer cost; the English adds that it is new.

column1: 这名男子抢走了她的包包。
column2: The man robbed her bag.
column4: “Robbed her bag” is not idiomatic; the man snatched or stole her bag.

column2: placeholder-p10
column4: The English is a placeholder, not a translation.

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” does not translate the Chinese sentence.

column2: How much is this racket?
column4: “块” is not a natural classifier for a racket; say “这把球拍” or “这个球拍”.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not an English translation.

column1: 这座建筑物将在城市建造。
column2: This building will be built in the city.
column4: “这座建筑物将在城市建造”表达不自然；可说“这座建筑物将在城市里建成”。

column2: I knew it!
column4: 这我知道 means “I know this,” not “I knew it.”

column2: That house is very small.
column4: 这房子 means “this house,” not “that house.”

column2: This room is used by teachers.
column4: “老师专用” means the room is reserved exclusively for teachers, not merely used by them.

column2: A typical example.
column4: The Chinese says “This is a typical example,” while the English is only a noun phrase.

column1: 这是一个历史性的决定。
column2: It was a historic decision.
column4: The Chinese says “This is a historic decision,” while the English says it was one.

column2: This is a misunderstanding.
column4: “一场误解” is unnatural; say “一个误解” or “一场误会.”

column1: 这是一幅他自己画的画。
column2: This is the picture of his own painting.
column4: The Chinese says he painted the picture himself; the English suggests a picture depicting his painting.

column2: Is it an Apple?
column4: “苹果” means the fruit here; “an Apple” refers to the company.

column1: 这是世界上最长的桥之一。
column2: One of the longest bridges in the world.
column4: The English is a fragment; it should say “This is one of the longest bridges in the world.”

column1: 这是什么地方？我们在这个地点见面。
column2: What place is this? Let's meet at this spot.
column4: The Chinese says “We meet at this spot,” not “Let’s meet at this spot.”

column2: This is his duty.
column4: “职务” means an official position or post, not a duty.

column2: Where did you get this?
column4: “这是你哪里拿的？” is not natural phrasing; say “这是你从哪里拿的？”

column2: Here is a letter for you.
column4: 这是你的信 means “This is your letter,” not “Here is a letter for you.”

column2: Is this typewriter yours?
column4: “Is this typewriter yours?”缺少冠词，应为“Is this a typewriter of yours?”或“Is this your typewriter?”

column2: This is the very book you wanted.
column4: “你非常想要的书” means the book you wanted very much, not necessarily “the very book” (the exact book) you wanted.

column2: placeholder
column4: “Placeholder” is not a translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: placeholder
column4: “placeholder” is not an English translation of the Chinese sentence.

column2: It was an interesting debate.
column4: “这是” means “this is,” not “it was.”

column2: What an old book this is!
column4: “这是多古老的书本呀” is unnatural; a native speaker would say “这本书多古老啊” or “这是一本多么古老的书啊.”

column1: 这是多好的一件事，以至于我不吐不快。
column2: It is such a nice thing to say that I felt the need to say it.
column4: The Chinese says it is such a good thing that the speaker must say something; the English says it is a nice thing to say.

column2: A show the public loves.
column4: “A show the public loves” is a sentence fragment.

column1: 这是对他们来说相当容易。
column2: It was rather easy for them.
column4: “这是对他们来说” is unnatural; say “这对他们来说相当容易.” The English also uses past tense, while the Chinese is present.

column2: It's a very serious illness.
column4: “病”通常需要量词，这里更自然地说“这是一种很严重的病”或“这是一场很严重的病”。

column2: This is my school.
column4: “我们的学校” means “our school,” not “my school.”

column1: 这是我的马马和我的爸爸。
column2: This is my mum and my dad.
column4: “马马” is incorrect here; it should be “妈妈”.

column1: 这是我读过的书里面写的最差的一本了。
column2: This is the worst book I've ever read.
column4: The Chinese describes the worst-written book, while the English calls it the worst book overall.

column2: Are these library books?
column4: “这是是” repeats 是; also, the Chinese is singular while the English is plural.

column2: This is from her.
column4: 这是来自她的 is unnatural Chinese; a native speaker would more naturally say 这是她给的 or 这是她寄来的.

column2: This is a serious medicine.
column4: “重药” is not a natural way to describe serious or potent medicine; “强效药” or “猛药” would be more idiomatic.

column2: That’s the first point.
column4: “这” means “this,” while the English says “that.”

column2: This is the third games.
column4: “The third games” is unnatural; say “the third edition of the games” or “the third sports meet.”

column2: placeholder-p8
column4: “placeholder-p8” is not an English translation.

column2: This is a pocket dictionary.
column4: “袖珍的字典” is awkward; a native speaker would usually say “袖珍字典”.

column2: Do you know whose this is?
column4: 这是谁的你知道吗 is awkwardly ordered; say 你知道这是谁的吗？

column2: Beauty beyond description.
column4: The English is a fragment, not a complete sentence.

column2: It concerns you.
column4: “这有关于你” is not a natural way to say “It concerns you.” Say “这和你有关” or “这关系到你.”

column1: 这本书不是给年轻读者看的。
column2: These books are not fit for young readers.
column4: 这本书是单数，英文的“These books”是复数。

column1: 这本书关于生活在英国。
column2: This book deals with life in the United Kingdom.
column4: The sentence is missing a construction such as “是” or “讲述”; as written, “这本书关于……” is ungrammatical.

column2: This book has many layers.
column4: “这本书分了很多层次”不太自然；通常会说书分成了很多部分或章节。

column2: This book will be printed next year.
column4: “出版” means “be published,” not specifically “be printed.”

column1: 这本汉语书对我们来说没有太难。
column2: This Chinese book is not too difficult for us.
column4: “没有太难” is awkward in this sentence; “不太难” or “没有那么难” is more natural.

column1: 这条村的东西比我们村的便宜多了。
column2: The things in this village are cheaper than those in ours.
column4: “这条村”不是自然的普通话说法；通常说“这个村”。

column2: This river is wide.
column4: 阔 is not the natural word for describing a river's width; use 宽.

column2: This road is closed.
column4: “这条路不通” means the road is impassable or doesn’t lead through, not necessarily that it is closed.

column2: This road is wide.
column4: “路很广” is an unnatural collocation; a road is usually described as “很宽.”

column2: No passage on this road.
column4: “No passage on this road” is unnatural English; “No through traffic” would be more natural.

column2: This passage is narrow.
column4: “很长” means “very long,” not “narrow.”

column1: 这架飞机完美的著陆了。
column2: The plane made a perfect landing.
column4: 完美的着陆了 uses 的 incorrectly; it should be 完美地着陆了.

column2: Do it like this, right?
column4: “Do it like this, right?” is awkward as a confirmation question; “Doing it like this is right, isn’t it?” would be natural.

column2: placeholder-p7
column4: “placeholder-p7” is not an English translation.

column2: Was the soup tasty?
column4: The Chinese asks whether the soup is tasty now; the English asks whether it was tasty.

column2: These medicines should be taken three times a day.
column4: 这点药 refers to an amount of medicine, not multiple medicines.

column1: 这片小区的绿地面积有多少？
column2: What is the size of this district's greenery area?
column4: “Greenery area” is not a natural English expression here; “green space” would be more idiomatic.

column2: This cat is very fat.
column4: “这猫是很肥”不自然；通常说“这只猫很肥”。

column1: 这男人是个语言学家，他自然知道。
column2: This man is a linguist. It's natural that he know.
column4: “It's natural that he know” is ungrammatical; it should be “It's natural that he knows” or “It's natural that he would know.”

column1: 这男孩第一次骑在马上。
column2: This boy is riding a horse for the first time.
column4: “第一次骑在马上” is unnatural here; say “这男孩第一次骑马。”

column2: This soup is too salty to eat.
column4: “大咸” is not grammatical here; say “太咸了”.

column1: 这碗汤的味道尝起来很奇怪。
column2: This soup tastes strange.
column4: “味道” and “尝起来” are awkward together. Say “这碗汤尝起来很奇怪” or “这碗汤的味道很奇怪。”

column2: These kind of things are the most troublesome.
column4: “These kind” is ungrammatical; say “these kinds” or “this kind.”

column1: 这药可以治疗你的皮肤病。
column2: This medicine will cure you of your skin disease.
column4: “可以治疗” means the medicine can treat the condition, not that it will cure it.

column1: 这药对我没有任何好处。
column2: The medicine didn't do me any good.
column4: The Chinese says the medicine does no good for me, while the English says it did no good in the past.

column1: 这蛋糕吃起来不同一般。
column2: The cake tastes divine!
column4: “吃起来不同一般”不自然；可说“这蛋糕吃起来非同一般”。

column2: You ain't seen nothing yet.
column4: 这还算什么！ means something like “What is this?” or “This is nothing!”; it does not mean “You ain't seen nothing yet.”

column2: This answer is correct.
column4: “这道题”指这道题目/问题，不是“this answer.”

column1: 这部电影为她赢得了人气。
column2: The movie gained her great popularity.
column4: “为她赢得了人气” is unnatural phrasing; the movie would typically be said to have made her more popular.

column2: This movie is starting to get really interesting.
column4: “有起意思来” is not a natural Chinese expression; use “开始有意思起来” or “变得有意思了.”

column1: 这里交通很方便，坐车十分钟就到。
column2: Transport here is convenient; ten minutes by bus.
column4: “Ten minutes by bus” is a fragment; it omits that you can get there in ten minutes.

column2: It's hot out here.
column4: 够热 means “hot enough,” not simply “hot.”

column2: It's warm in here.
column4: “这里是温暖的” is unnatural for describing the temperature; say “这里很暖和”.

column2: Anyone here knows how to drive?
column4: 疑问句应说“Does anyone here know how to drive?”

column2: PH
column4: “PH”不是可理解的英文翻译。

column1: 这里被列为重点保护区。
column2: Listed as a key protected zone.
column4: “Listed as a key protected zone” is a fragment, not a complete sentence.

column2: placeholder-p12
column4: “placeholder-p12”不是英文句子。

column1: 这里面我有很多不懂的。
column2: I don't understand much about it.
